threadSnapshot.title: fix(body): match form content type case-insensitively in `readBody`
threadSnapshot.body:
`readBody()` decides whether to parse the body as url-encoded with a case-sensitive `startsWith("application/x-www-form-urlencoded")`. Media types are case-insensitive (RFC 9110, section 8.3.1: "The type and subtype tokens are case-insensitive."), so a request with a differently cased type falls through to `JSON.parse` and gets a 400:

```js
app.post("/", (event) => readBody(event));
```

```
$ curl -s localhost:3000 -H 'content-type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' -d 'a=1&b=2'
{"a":"1","b":"2"}
$ curl -s localhost:3000 -H 'content-type: Application/x-www-form-urlencoded' -d 'a=1&b=2'
{"status":400,"statusText":"Bad Request","message":"Invalid JSON body"}
```

`readBody(event, { type: "formData" })` already accepts the same request, since `Request.formData()` parses the header case-insensitively, so the default path was the odd one out.

The fix lowercases the header before the check. The new test sends two differently cased form content types (one with a `charset` parameter) through the web and node matrix; without the source change both fail with `expected { status: 400, ... } to deeply equal { field: 'value', ... }`.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * URL-encoded form bodies are now parsed correctly when the `Content-Type` header uses uppercase or mixed-case letters, including with a charset parameter.

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

threadSnapshot.title: docs: fix file paths in static assets example
threadSnapshot.body:
Resolves #1578

The "Read files" example mounts the handler at `/public/**`, but `serveStatic` passes the full request path as `id` (e.g. `/public/index.html`). So `join("public", id)` looks for `public/public/index.html` and every request returns 404. The text also says to open `http://localhost:3000`, which isn't matched by `/public/**`.

Changes:
- Strip the `/public` prefix from `id` before joining it with the directory.
- Point readers to `http://localhost:3000/public/`, after the full example.

I checked both versions against h3 2.0.2 with a `public/index.html` file:

| Path | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/` | 404 | 404 (outside the mount, expected) |
| `/public/` | 404 | 200 |
| `/public/index.html` | 404 | 200 |

* **Documentation**
  * Updated the static assets example to show creating `public/index.html` before opening `/public/` in a browser.
  * Clarified that `/public` is removed from request paths before they’re used to read files or look up file metadata.

threadSnapshot.title: fix(static): normalize indexNames path join with single boundary slash
threadSnapshot.body:
<!--
Thank you for reporting an issue.

The issue tracker is for reporting bugs and discussing features.
-->

### 🔗 Linked issue

Closes #1584

### ❓ Type of change

- [x] 📖 Documentation (updates to the documentation, readme or JSdoc annotations)
- [x] 🐞 Bug fix (a non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] 👌 Enhancement (improving an existing functionality like performance)
- [ ] ✨ New feature (a non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🧹 Chore (updates to the build process or auxiliary tools and libraries)
- [ ] ⚠️ Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change)

### 📚 Description

When serving static index files, `idSearchPaths` previously constructed candidate asset IDs by simple string concatenation: `${id}${suffix}`.

Because `originalId` for root `GET /` retains a leading slash (`withoutTrailingSlash("/") === "/"`):
1. **Root double slash with default `indexNames: ["/index.html"]`**:
   Concatenating `"/"` and `"/index.html"` resulted in `"//index.html"`. This non-canonical path fails canonical path lookup and asset table lookup in storage backends, returning a `404` for root index requests.
2. **Missing directory separator with relative `indexNames: ["index.html"]`**:
   When configuring relative index names without a leading slash, requesting a subdirectory like `GET /docs` concatenated `"/docs"` and `"index.html"`, producing `"/docsindex.html"`.

This fix normalizes index name boundary joining:
```ts
const assetId = suffix ? `${id.replace(/\/+$/, "")}/${suffix.replace(/^\/+/, "")}` : id;
```
Ensuring a single slash boundary regardless of whether `id` is `"/"` or a subdirectory, and whether `suffix` contains a leading slash.

### 📝 Checklist

- [x] I have linked an issue or discussion.
- [x] I have updated the documentation accordingly.
- [x] I have added tests to cover my changes.
